title: Injection injury prevention and site exclusion
audience: Trainees and workers on the pressure cleaning (all heights) track, and supervisors who set exclusion zones. Completing this lesson does not give competency to operate high-pressure water jetting equipment.
learningOutcomes: Explain why a high-pressure water jet is a serious injection hazard even when the entry wound looks small.
Apply the personal protective equipment and exclusion controls that the WorkSafe Victoria jetting alert describes for routine work.
Stop work and seek urgent medical attention when a jet injury or hose failure occurs.

instruction.heading: Why injection injury is different
instruction.body: A high-pressure water jet can penetrate skin and drive water, dirt or other material into the tissue beneath. The wound at the surface can look minor, while the damage underneath may be much larger, and the material carried into the body may be contaminated. WorkSafe Victoria's high-pressure water jetting safety alert (published 14 September 2022, reviewed 11 May 2023) warns that a jet can puncture the skin and drive contaminated material into the body. The alert gives no first-aid step. Treat any skin contact with a jet as a reason for urgent medical attention.

instruction.heading: Immediate response to a jet injury
instruction.body: If a jet strikes a person, stop the equipment at once and isolate it as the manufacturer directs. Tell the medical team that the injury was caused by a high-pressure water jet, and tell them what the jet may have carried, such as detergent, dirt or other material from the surface being cleaned. Do not wait to see whether the injury gets worse. Record the time, the equipment, the operator and the witnesses, and report the incident as the employer's procedure requires. Keep the injured person still and call for urgent medical attention.

instruction.heading: Keep hands and body away from the jet
instruction.body: Never check a nozzle, a spray pattern or a blockage with a hand or any part of the body while the equipment is pressurised. Do not place a hand in front of the wand to test the flow. Before clearing a blockage, changing a nozzle or working on a coupling, isolate the equipment and release the pressure as the manufacturer's instructions direct. Keep the wand pointed at the surface being cleaned at all times, and keep the operator's own feet and legs clear of the line of the jet.

instruction.heading: Exclusion zones and site control
instruction.body: Set an exclusion zone around the work area before the equipment starts. Keep people, pets and vehicles out of the zone, and use barriers, cones or a supervisor to hold it. Stop the jet immediately when anyone enters the zone, and restart only when the zone is clear. Where the site is shared with other workers or the public, agree the zone with the site controller and record the agreement. The zone must cover the spray, the splash and the path of any loose debris.

instruction.heading: Personal protective equipment
instruction.body: The WorkSafe Victoria alert (reviewed 11 May 2023) says anyone close to jetting operations needs eye protection, and that the operator who controls the water flow wears at least safety glasses with a face shield. Head protection applies where the risk calls for it. Armour for the legs and body, able to take the jet's full force, is needed where injury is possible, and ear protection is needed where noise cannot be reduced. Check the PPE before every job and replace damaged items. The job pack should name the PPE for the task, and a worker who lacks the required PPE does not start the jet.

instruction.heading: Hose failure and equipment condition
instruction.body: A flailing hose, an uncontrolled nozzle or a separated hose coupling can strike a person with force. Before use, check that every hose, fitting and coupling is compatible, correctly sized and rated no lower than the equipment's highest operating pressure, as the WorkSafe Victoria alert requires. Do not fit attachments or make changes that the manufacturer or a competent person has not approved in writing. Repair or maintenance should be left to the manufacturer, its agent or a competent person.

instruction.heading: Competency boundary
instruction.body: The WorkSafe Victoria alert (reviewed 11 May 2023) sorts jetting systems by output in bar litres per minute: Class A covers 800 to 5,600 and Class B covers output above 5,600. Class B operators need training and an assessment of competence delivered by a registered training organisation (RTO), and refresher sessions must be logged no less often than every two years. The alert relies on AS/NZS 4233.1:2013. Compare the stated output of any machine with these bands before deciding whether this applies. This lesson does not provide that competency.

instruction.heading: Licence and authority boundary
instruction.body: Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate, competency or authority to operate industrial or Class B water jetting equipment. The competency route described in the alert is provided by registered training organisations. Obtain the employer's written authorisation before any work with high-pressure equipment.

procedure: Set the exclusion zone and confirm with the site controller who holds it.
Check the PPE for the task and confirm the operator in control of the water flow wears at least safety glasses and a face shield.
Inspect every hose, fitting and coupling for damage, compatibility and a rating no lower than the maximum operating pressure.
Confirm no attachment is fitted without written approval from the manufacturer or a competent person, and that the equipment is the one described in the job pack.
Start the equipment only when the zone is clear, and keep the wand directed at the surface being cleaned.
Stop immediately if a person enters the zone, a hose or coupling moves unexpectedly, or the equipment behaves abnormally.
Isolate and release pressure before any adjustment or clearance, as the manufacturer directs.
If any person is struck, seek urgent medical attention, isolate the equipment, and record and report the incident.

workedExamples.situation: A worker sees a fine spray leaking from a hose connection close to the wand while cleaning a paved driveway. The operator has not stopped the equipment.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must the worker do first, and why?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the equipment and isolate it as the manufacturer directs before doing anything else. A leaking connection at high pressure can separate or spray with force. Keep people clear of the spray, release the pressure, and inspect the coupling. Do not restart until the fitting is repaired or replaced by a person authorised to do so. Record the defect and report it.

workedExamples.situation: A neighbour walks into the work area to ask a question and steps into the line of the jet, which is still running.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the jet at once, because the exclusion zone has been breached. Move the neighbour out of the zone, and check whether any water or material has struck them. If there is any sign of a jet injury, seek urgent medical attention, however small the mark appears. Restart only when the zone is clear and the supervisor has confirmed the controls.

equipmentAndPpe: Safety glasses and face shield for the operator in control of the water flow
Head protection, body and leg armour and hearing protection where the risk requires them
Barriers, cones and a supervisor to hold the exclusion zone
Hose, fitting and coupling inspection checklist with the maximum operating pressure of each part
Manufacturer instructions for isolation and release of pressure

commonErrors.error: Treating a small skin puncture from a jet as a minor cut.
commonErrors.prevention: Seek urgent medical attention for any jet contact and tell the medical team what the jet may have carried.

commonErrors.error: Checking the nozzle or spray pattern with a hand while the equipment is pressurised.
commonErrors.prevention: Isolate and release pressure before any inspection, adjustment or clearance.

commonErrors.error: Letting a passer-by or a co-worker enter the spray line.
commonErrors.prevention: Hold the exclusion zone with barriers or a supervisor and stop the jet when the zone is breached.

commonErrors.error: Using a hose or coupling that is damaged or not rated for the pressure.
commonErrors.prevention: Inspect every hose and coupling before use and remove any defective part from service.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Injection injury: the alert warns that a jet can puncture the skin and drive contaminated material into the body (published 14 September 2022, reviewed 11 May 2023).

PPE: the alert (reviewed 11 May 2023) says anyone close to jetting operations needs eye protection, and the operator who controls the water flow wears at least safety glasses with a face shield. Other PPE follows the risk.

Equipment: attachments and changes need written approval from the manufacturer or a competent person, and repair is for the manufacturer, its agent or a competent person (WorkSafe Victoria alert, reviewed 11 May 2023).

Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate, competency or authority to operate Class B or industrial water jetting equipment. Class B operators must be trained and assessed as competent through a registered training organisation, with refresher training recorded at least every two years (WorkSafe Victoria alert, reviewed 11 May 2023).

qualityStandard: The exclusion zone is set and held before the equipment starts.
The PPE for the task is checked and worn by the operator in control of the water flow.
Every hose, fitting and coupling is inspected and rated for the maximum operating pressure.
No attachment is fitted without written approval, and the equipment is stopped at once for any breach or defect.
documentationEvidence: Exclusion zone record with the person who holds it
PPE check record for each worker
Hose, fitting and coupling inspection record with the rated pressure
Incident record for any jet contact or hose failure, with the medical response and the report
summary: A high-pressure jet can inject material beneath the skin, and the surface wound can understate the injury.
Never check a jet with a hand, and isolate and release pressure before any work on the equipment.
Hold the exclusion zone, and stop the jet when anyone enters it.
This lesson does not grant competency or authority to operate Class B equipment.

knowledgeChecks.question: A high-pressure jet has touched a worker's hand and left only a small mark. What is the correct response?
options: Clean and cover the mark, then keep working, since the mark is small and the hand is fine
Wait to see if it gets worse before seeking help, since the mark is only small and looks clean
Apply a bandage and finish the job, since the bandage will hold the mark closed for the day
Stop the equipment and seek urgent medical attention, telling the medical team about the jet

knowledgeChecks.question: A nozzle is blocked. What must happen before the worker clears it?
options: Isolate the equipment and release the pressure as the manufacturer directs
Clear it with a hand while the jet runs, since the jet is weak at the tip
Turn the pressure up to clear it quickly and then drop it again
Clear it while a helper holds the wand steady for the worker today

knowledgeChecks.question: Which PPE does the WorkSafe Victoria alert state the operator in control of the water flow must wear at least?
options: Gloves and a hat and work boots
Safety glasses and a face shield
A dust mask and nothing else
Ear plugs and nothing else at all

knowledgeChecks.question: A passer-by walks into the spray line during a job. What is the first step?
options: Keep working and warn them verbally to step aside
Ask them to step back while the jet runs
Stop the jet at once and hold the exclusion zone
Increase the pressure to clear them out of the spray line

knowledgeChecks.question: Does completing this lesson give competency to operate Class B equipment?
options: Yes, for residential jobs, since the work is small
Yes, once the quiz is passed by the worker on the day
Yes, if the employer agrees to it in writing for the job
No, the lesson grants no competency, licence or authority

officialReferences.covers: Not confirmed by an official source: no official first aid guidance for high-pressure jet injection was found.
